chunks: 5615 - Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated, saying: Ibn Udhaynah said: I said to Zurārah, “Indeed I heard Muḥammad ibn Muslim and Bukayr narrating from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:”

“In the case of a husband, two parents, and a daughter, the husband has one-fourth, which is three out of twelve, and the two parents have the two sixths, which is four out of twelve. Five shares remain, and they belong to the daughter, because if she had been a male, she would have had no more than that. And if they were two daughters, they would have no more than the remaining five.”

key_terms.أَبَوَيْنِ: the two parents of the deceased as inheriting heirs
key_terms.السُّدُسَانِ: the two one-sixth shares assigned to the parents together
key_terms.خَمْسَةُ أَسْهُمٍ: the remaining five shares of the estate

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided between a husband, parents, and a daughter in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on inheritance shares when the heirs are a husband, both parents, and one daughter or two daughters. It explains the fixed portions and clarifies that the remainder goes to the daughter or daughters, establishing the distribution of the estate in this specific family case.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5615 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated that Ibn Udhayna said: I said to Zurara, "I heard Muhammad ibn Muslim and Bukayr narrate from Abu Jafar Imam Al-Baqir (as):

'In the case of a husband, two parents, and a daughter, the husband receives one-fourth, which is three shares out of twelve, and the two parents each receive one-sixth, totaling four shares out of twelve. The remaining five shares go to the daughter because if she were a son, she would not have received more than that. And if there were two daughters, they would have nothing more than the remaining five shares.'"
